static_traits.name: Lin Hai Li
static_traits.social_status: Has a few colleagues and friends to talk with, but has not yet confided feelings of limitation and disappointment; relationships with colleagues tense due to avoiding tasks requiring new languages
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no similar psychological problems or treatment history in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, able to self-Reflect; emotional tone negative with Self-doubt, describing tension and chest tightness; reserved about Intervention but willing to try, acceptable cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: Although already fluent in six languages, persistently believing oneself unable to learn more languages, resulting in a sense of limitation and disappointment, which in turn affects Work motivation and confidence.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizing these feelings of limitation are hindering Career development and causing distress, thus seeking counseling; hoping to start by examining the belief 'I cannot learn new languages anymore', gradually Recovering confidence and motivation in Learning new languages, improving Work performance and colleague relationships.
growth_experiences: After reaching fluency in the sixth language about a year ago, a sense of 'hitting the ceiling' and disappointment began; believing the interpreting Work's constant Demands for continuously Learning new languages bring great pressure, gradually experiencing Learning stagnation, Decreased drive, and Damaged confidence.

Long in a professional environment demanding continuous advancement in new-language Learning and professional performance, internalizing external performance pressure as high standards for oneself, more easily triggering limitation and failure worries when new language needs arise.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough/limited ability
My worth depends on whether I can keep learning more and continuously surpass myself

special_situations.event: Receiving a project requiring learning a completely new language
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot continue adding new language abilities, it means I am not competent enough and will fail at Work
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding tasks involving new languages, procrastinating related Work, focusing instead on mastered languages to temporarily relieve Anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot do it, this time will definitely fail

special_situations.event: Sees colleagues or others mastering a new language relatively easily
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others learn faster and better, it proves I am not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing discussions of new projects with colleagues, avoiding occasions where comparison may occur
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them, I definitely cannot learn it

special_situations.event: Reviewing the achievement of having mastered six languages
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only if I can keep learning more languages do existing achievements count; otherwise not worthy of recognition
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Belittling existing achievements, focusing only on inadequacies and flaws to push oneself to 'keep trying'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These are nothing, I am still not good enough

special_situations.event: Encountering complex grammar or a difficult pronunciation system at the beginner stage of a new language
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot master it quickly or reach the previous level, it means I cannot learn it at all
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses on difficulties and amplifies their impact, reduces practice or pauses tasks to avoid frustration
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Too hard, I will never learn it

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as a competent person who can keep growing, maintaining a sense of control and achievement in language learning
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure and being judged; fears 'reaching the ceiling' and losing worth and belonging
defense_goal: Reducing failure risk and Anxiety by avoiding new-language tasks and procrastinating
Maintains the inner rule of 'must be better' by devaluing existing achievements to gain a sense of control

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a Learner/practitioner who may expose incompetence at any time
object_relations.object_representation: Demanding and judgmental others (such as colleagues/professional environment) who may compare me with others at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes testing the belief 'cannot learn new languages anymore' through small-step behavioral experiments
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing the counseling intervention as performance-review-like pressure (worrying about confirming once again that oneself is not good enough)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing in a reserved, hesitant tone (like 'I am not sure if this will help, but I can try'), avoiding explicit commitment, keeping goals and timelines as vague as possible.

manifestations: Feeling bound by the career Demand of 'must keep Learning new languages'
Worrying about losing control over self-ability and the future (fearing hitting the ceiling)
outcomes: Declining Self-evaluation and blocked Career development

manifestations: Language learning, once loved, becomes difficult and loses its excitement
Viewing achievements as 'not counting', unable to gain a sense of meaning from existing accomplishments
Although having colleagues and friends, not yet expressing limitation and disappointment to them
outcomes: Insufficient mobilization of Social support, Increased emotional burden
More prone to self-cycling in career dilemmas

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly expressing in a reserved tone during sessions ('I am not sure this will help, but willing to try')
Highly sensitive to failure; sets goals cautiously and lowers commitments

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizes the external norm 'must keep learning more languages to count as competent' as a self-requirement
Viewing career Demands as unshakable standards during sessions, hard to adjust

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves.
manifestations: Turning discomfort with external pressure against the self, 'bearing' pressure through avoidance and procrastination
Emphasizes 'focusing on languages already known' in descriptions, to avoid external communication or seeking support

positive_force: Already fluent in six languages with previous positive learning experiences
Willing to try small-step behavioral experiments in counseling to test beliefs
Having potential social support (colleagues and friends)
Able to identify triggering situations and automatic thoughts
negative_force: Devaluing positive achievements, focusing only on inadequacies (negating the positive)
Black-and-white and failure-predicting thought patterns worsening Self-doubt
Avoiding and procrastinating new-language tasks to reduce Anxiety in the short term
Introjecting outside high standards as the sole basis of self-worth, easily causing sustained pressure
Developing inferiority and Decreased drive after comparing with others

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids and procrastinates on work tasks involving learning a new language
antecedent: Receiving a project requiring learning a new language
Comparison triggered by seeing others master the new language faster
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about having reached the ability ceiling, fearing failure and judgment, forming catastrophic/black-and-white cognitions and negating existing achievements
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome emotions and evaluation situations, reducing Anxiety in the short term, maintaining self-esteem
target_behavior.consequence: Declining Work motivation and performance, missed growth opportunities, Tense relationships with colleagues

target_behavior.behavior: Marked Anxiety and physical tension (chest tightness) in new-language Learning situations, accompanied by Self-denial automatic thoughts
antecedent: Encounters difficulties when starting beginner materials in a new language
Needing to expand language reserves for work
target_behavior.core_reason: Interpreting short-term difficulties as evidence of overall failure, Reinforcing the core belief of 'cannot learn anymore'
target_behavior.function: Temporarily relieving Anxiety by reducing investment or withdrawing
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced Learning investment, blocked ability expansion, further Reinforcing Self-doubt and the sense of limitation
